headline: Your growth plate
body: It doesn't just receive hormones. It has the enzymes to rebuild them on site.
punch: And it splits testosterone down two paths with opposite effects.

headline: Path one
body: Aromatase converts testosterone into estradiol. Researchers detected aromatase transcripts by RT-PCR directly in human growth plate tissue, taken from adolescents during epiphysiodesis surgery, and localised the protein in the plate.
punch: Human tissue. Not a mouse, not a cell line.

headline: And the plate
body: A human chondrocyte cell line both produced 17 beta estradiol and responded to it, changing proliferation and apoptosis. That's a complete local loop: the tissue makes the hormone and reads it.
punch: It manufactures its own closure signal.

headline: That estradiol
body: Estrogen acting on estrogen receptors in chondrocytes drives skeletal maturation and eventual fusion. This is why aromatisation matters so much: the closing hormone is being made inside the tissue it closes.
punch: Blood estradiol underestimates what your plate is exposed to.

headline: Path two
body: Human fetal epiphyseal cartilage metabolises testosterone directly, and cultured human epiphyseal chondrocytes carry specific DHT binding sites. That means functional androgen receptors in the cartilage itself.
punch: The same tissue runs both enzymes.

headline: DHT cannot aromatise
body: DHT is a dead end for the estrogen pathway. Testosterone that becomes DHT can never become estradiol, so it acts on the androgen receptor without feeding the closure signal.
punch: One path builds. The other path ends you.

headline: Which is why
body: Oxandrolone in paediatric growth disorders produced growth velocity of 4.5 to 9.6 cm per year and 2.3 to 4.6 cm of additional adult height across 45 studies. That is not what a compound that closes plates does.
punch: The evidence is in constitutional delay, Turner syndrome and burns.

headline: But the same review
body: Skeletal maturation still advanced 3 to 7 months, and adverse effects were dose dependent, clustering above 0.06 mg per kg per day. Virilisation appeared in 12.5 to 15.2% at those higher doses.
punch: Low dose gained height. High dose spent bone age.

headline: So the usable point
body: How much testosterone becomes estradiol versus DHT at the plate decides whether you are growing or closing. That split shifts with dose and age, and it happens locally, where no blood test can see it.
punch: Ask what it becomes, not how much you took.

headline: It's never over
body: Real mechanisms, real citations, no protocols.
